references.text: The priest who offers the sin offering shall eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the tent of meeting. This explains why Moses expected the sin offering goat to be eaten.

But any sin offering whose blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place must not be eaten; it must be burned with fire. This provides the background for the rules concerning the sin offering.
The Israelites were commanded to take a male goat as a sin offering. This is the same sin offering goat that Moses was looking for.
Aaron presented the people's offerings and took the male goat as a sin offering. This shows the offering that Moses later examined.
Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord. Their death explains why Eleazar and Ithamar were the remaining sons of Aaron.
Moses gave instructions to Aaron and his remaining sons about eating the offerings. This provides the context for Moses' anger that the sin offering was burned.
The meat of the bull, its skin and its dung you shall burn with fire outside the camp. It is a sin offering. This shows earlier instructions regarding the burning of the sin offering.
Eleazar and Ithamar are mentioned as Aaron's sons who served as priests. This confirms their role as the remaining priests.
